newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Supermarket group Ahold's profits jump.
newsitem.headline: Supermarket group Ahold's profits jump.

text.p: Dutch supermarket giant Ahold NV impressed investors with an 18 percent rise in second quarter net profits on Thursday and promised more good news as recently acquired U.S.-based Stop & Shop proves a better deal then expected.

"Everything that has happened in the first half year is mind boggling," Ahold president Cees van der Hoeven told a news conference. "We're on our way to becoming the largest worldwide supermarket group."

The group earlier announced second quarter net profit of 121.3 million guilders, up from 102.5 million in the same period in 1995 and at the top end of analysts' expectations of between 111 and 123 million guilders.
Ahold was upbeat about future prospects, reiterating an earlier forecast that, excluding Stop & Shop, net profit in 1996 would be higher than that in 1995.

Van der Hoeven said the Stop & Shop deal alone, to be consolidated as of the third quarter 1996 and partly funded by the issue of 39.3 million new shares, would directly improve group earnings per share.
"At this moment it seems the acquisition of Stop & Shop will directly lead to an improvement in EPS, even after the recent major share issue," he said.

The acquisition will result in a "significant increase in sales, operating results and net earnings," Ahold said, though goodwill write-off will initially have an acceptable negative impact on the equity ratio.

Van der Hoeven said the second quarter results were given a boost from the stronger dollar versus the guilder, but added that underlying growth in operating profit was nevertheless substantial and in line with long-term forecasts.
Operating profit rose 21 percent to 243.6 million guilders, with the increase slipping to 16.2 percent at constant rates.
Analysts welcomed the results. "They look quite good," said Bangert Pontier analyst Paul Schram. "Noteable was that the sales figures were even stronger than I expected."
Consolidated sales in guilder terms rose 15.8 percent to 7.8 billion guilders in the second quarter.
Sales rose a healthy 27.8 percent in other European countries, namely Portugal and the Czech Republic.
In the U.S., sales rose by 14 percent to $2.1 billion and operating profit by 20.7 percent to $61.3 million.

"In the U.S. there was quite a strong rebound in profitablilty," said Schram. "In the first quarter margins were flat compared to last year, in Q2 they were up 0.1 pct versus the same period in 1995. That was better than I expected."

Ahold USA president Rob Zwartendijk was upbeat about the Stop & Shop acquisition. "There have been no negative surprises. Things are working out better than expected, to put it mildly," he said. "We are looking forward to exploiting the great many synergies there."
Van der Hoeven said the recently announced reorganisation within Ahold USA -- the merger of Finast with Tops and that of Edwards and Giant -- would result in 400 job losses in total.
The axe will fall among the 900 workers at the head offices of Edwards in Long Island and Finast in Cleveland which are both to be closed.
Ahold is the fourth largest retailer in the U.S. with 800 stores generating annual turnover of $14 billion, more than half of total group turnover.

Zwartendijk said Ahold was still on the lookout for acquisitions on the East coast of the U.S. "We're not going to look at the West coast because we wouldn't be able to exploit synergies from there," he said.
Investors signalled their approval of the deal, pushing the shares to close up 0.30 guilders at 93.30.
